stem.en: Hydrogen sulphide is sulphur with two hydrogens. Sulphur, like oxygen, has six outer electrons. What shape is it?

text.en: Bent. Sulphur has two shared pairs and two lone pairs, four groups, and you see two corners.

feedback.en: The two lone pairs on the sulphur push the hydrogens down into a bend, exactly as in water.
Shape is counted at the central atom. Sulphur has four groups around it, two of them lone pairs.
The four groups are arranged tetrahedrally, but the shape you name is the shape the atoms make. Two visible corners out of four is called bent.

explanation.en: Same column as oxygen, same count of outer electrons, same groups, same bent shape. The table you built in I.5 predicts shapes as well as families.
